small_guidance:
- The kernel currently launches one program per (N, OH, OW-tile) with BLOCK_M = next_pow2(OC) = 64 — that's fine, but BLOCK_N tiles only along OW (width=126). Add configs that fuse OH*OW into a single spatial axis so each program covers a larger contiguous chunk and the grid (N*OH = 128*126 = 16128) isn't so skewed; also try BLOCK_M=32 with two OC tiles to relax register pressure and unlock BLOCK_N=128/256 with num_stages=3.
- K_FLAT = 8*3*3 = 72 gets rounded to 128, wasting 43% of the inner-product work. Pad weight/x along IC to IC=16 (so K_FLAT=144 → pad to 256? no — just compute exact K_FLAT=72 with masked loads on `offs_k < K_FLAT`), or special-case K_FLAT as the literal compile-time constant 72 via a constexpr that's not next_pow2 — tl.dot can accept BLOCK_K=16 with an inner Python loop of cdiv(72,16)=5 iterations, removing wasted FMAs.
- Add an autotune config with BLOCK_N=32, num_warps=2 to cover the OW-tail edge case and one with num_stages=4 for the large BLOCK_N=256 case to hide global-load latency on the per-pixel x gather.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as an im2col-style GEMM with one program per (N, OC_tile, OHW_tile) where OHW = OH*OW is flattened. Loop over K = IC*KH*KW with BLOCK_K=16 or 32, accumulating with tl.dot — this gives a real M=OC(64) × N=OHW_tile(64-128) × K=72 GEMM per program and a much flatter, larger grid (N * cdiv(OHW,BN) = 128 * ~250 ≈ 32k programs) than the current N*OH*cdiv(OW,BN) layout, improving SM occupancy.
- Switch the input layout to NHWC (channels_last) so the K-dimension reduction loads contiguous IC values per (h,w); the current NCHW gather strides by IH*IW across IC and hurts L1 throughput. Keep weight as (OC, KH*KW*IC) to match.
- Fuse the bias+scale epilogue (already done) and drop the runtime padding-to-next-pow2 of OC/IC — since OC=64 and IC=8 are constants at eval, hard-code BLOCK_M=64 and use a small inner K-loop with BLOCK_K=16 over the true K_FLAT=72 with a mask on the last iteration. This eliminates the ~78% wasted K-work (72/128) the current kernel performs.
